Definition: Micajah, the name of two Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Three different men answer to this name, and the Bible keeps them apart by their stories. One is the royal official Josiah sends to consult Huldah when the Book of the Law is found, one is the prophet Micah whose words Jeremiah's elders quote a century later, and one is a priest who sounds a trumpet at the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the shared name is a small warning against blurring people together: each Micajah stands in his own place, and God deals with each one there.
RelatedEvents: Josiah Finds the Book of the Law; The Dedication of Jerusalem's Wall
